lines.text: It came from Hatch 3.
From a room with *no* *air.*
I didn't move. I didn't breathe.
I just floated there with a flashlight, staring at a door that had nothing behind it.
The gauge still said zero.
I didn't sleep again that night.
In the morning, I called Ground on channel 4.
Ground, I heard knocking. From Module 3.
For the first time in forty days, Ground said more than three words.
Thermal expansion. Ignore it. Continue.
And that's real. One lap around the Earth takes ninety minutes.
Forty-five in the sun. Forty-five in the shadow. The metal heats up, cools down, and creaks.
But metal doesn't knock *three* *times.*
Day forty-one. Three in the morning.
Knock. Knock. Knock.
Day forty-two. Three in the morning.
Knock. Knock. Knock.
Every night. Exactly at three.
So I did the math on the oxygen.
At 1.7 kilos a day, the tank would be empty on day 186.
The next ship comes on day 365.
Day sixty. Envelope two.
If the numbers and Ground ever disagree, trust the numbers.
The numbers said someone was breathing.
Ground said I was alone.
Day sixty-one. Two fifty-nine in the morning.
This time I was awake. Waiting at the hatch.
Three o'clock came. Nothing.
Then at three-oh-seven, the knocks came back.
But they were different.
Three short. Three long. Three short.
And I knew *exactly* what it meant.
